paragraphs: Friend, here's what this passage teaches: pride is dangerous, and the way out is to listen. Jeremiah opens with "Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant, for the LORD has spoken." (Jeremiah 13:15) Notice what he asks for first. He asks them to give glory to the LORD their God before the darkness comes (Jeremiah 13:16). When the LORD has spoken, the wise thing is to hear Him while there's still time.

Now look at the prophet himself. He says that if they won't listen, "I will weep in secret because of your pride." (Jeremiah 13:17) I think that's the part to hold onto. The truth is hard, but the one telling it is crying over it, and I think that tells you how God's word comes to us. Then comes the question, "Can the Ethiopian change his skin, or the leopard his spots?" (Jeremiah 13:23) The people were so used to evil that they couldn't just turn around on their own.

So what does that mean for you, baker? We can't talk ourselves out of our own habits, and the LORD says the trouble came because they had "forgotten Me and trusted in falsehood." (Jeremiah 13:25) He ends with a question, "How long will you remain unclean?" (Jeremiah 13:27) That question is still hanging there, and the story isn't over. Stay humble, keep listening to the LORD, and remember Him, because nothing else can change what's inside us.
